findings.issue: USER_REFERRAL_IP_HASH_SALT and USER_REFERRAL_IP_LOOKBACK changed from '-' to 'helm' in the Set-in column. The chart does not set either one. deploy/local/scripts/env-reference.mjs (inHelm, a word match over values.yaml and the templates) picks up the names from the new comment in values.yaml:55-56. So the reference now says the AWS chart sets the salt, which contradicts TD-P8-24 (remediation-plan row 55, still open: the salt is not wired through Helm). An operator could believe the salt is provisioned when every replica actually hashes with its own random key.
findings.fix: In the values.yaml comment, refer to the settings by property name (user.referral.ip-lookback, user.referral.ip-hash-salt) or by 'the referral lookback and salt settings' instead of the env names. Alternatively, make inHelm skip comment lines. Then regenerate environment-variables.md so both rows show '-' again.

findings.issue: Prior nit 2 (s1r2) is still open. The bounded-deviation list still leaves out that an empty right-hand XFF entry (trailing comma, '1.1.1.1,') now falls back to the peer instead of resolving.
findings.fix: Add one bullet to the Consequences deviation list and to the PR description.

findings.issue: Stale wording. It still says the gateway's stripping 'stops user-service seeing the real client IP, which is why USER_REFERRAL_IP_LOOKBACK defaults to 0 (backlog B-1)'. After this change the IP arrives via X-Internal-Client-Ip, and the default stays off because of hop confirmation and B-4.
findings.fix: Reword it to say the client IP now arrives via X-Internal-Client-Ip (B-1) and that the remaining TD-SEC-15 scope is the OIDC forwarded host/proto only.

findings.issue: Only the gateway (Helm) and user-service (application.yml:105) pin forward-headers-strategy to none. auth-service and payment-service keep Boot's Kubernetes default NATIVE, so the getRemoteAddr() fallback in ClientIp is whatever Tomcat RemoteIpValve derives from X-Forwarded-For. This only matters when the header is absent: a direct in-cluster call, or the gateway removing the header for an unresolvable peer. That case is inside the documented in-cluster trust boundary, so the impact is low. But the ClientIp javadoc claim 'never reads X-Forwarded-For' does not hold end to end on those services.
findings.fix: Either set SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for every servlet service in the chart, or add one sentence to the ADR trust-boundary bullet about the peer fallback under NATIVE.

findings.issue: T14 asked for the Feign relay item in the techdebt register. It was filed in .openforge/knowledge/backlog.md and the ADR Consequences instead. CTO condition 6 is met in substance, but the item is not where the task said.
findings.fix: Optionally add a one-line pointer in docs/techdebt/README.md, or note in the PR that backlog.md is the record.

summary: Slice 2 (d195a937..b4abf171) meets AC-6 to AC-12. AC-1 to AC-5, AC-10 and AC-13 carry over from slice 1 and are re-confirmed by the CEO-run forge-verify recorded in evidence.md (PASS, 291 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failures, env reference --check PASS). The new common-web ClientIp trusts exactly one header line that parses, otherwise uses the parsed peer, otherwise empty/'unknown'. It never reads XFF and never throws. All five readers now use it: AuditInterceptor, WalletController (null when unknown, which GiftCardService already treats as 'no IP limit', so unknown callers do not share one bucket), auth RequestDeviceContext, AdminUserController (both call sites) and user-service EngageController. Grepping src/main finds no other X-Forwarded-For or getRemoteAddr reader outside ClientIp and GatewayClientIp. Duplication is resolved: user-service ClientIp and its test are deleted, and the parse cases already live in ClientAddressTest. The AUTH_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR flag is gone from AuthProperties, both application.yml blocks and the docs, and USER_REFERRAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS is gone from properties, yml, Helm and docs. The tests would catch a regression. The audit, wallet, admin and device-context tests each send the gateway header next to a conflicting X-Forwarded-For or socket peer, so the old code would fail them. The wallet test also covers rotating XFF (one bucket) and the null key. The referral MVC and real-Tomcat tests now drive the header and keep their assertions, and the lookback-0 tests are unchanged. Prior nit 1 is resolved: the zone guard is now lastIndexOf(':', zone) and '1.1.1.1%x:80' is in the rejects list. Prior nit 2 (the trailing-comma deviation in the ADR) is still open. Size: evidence.md records 474 production lines for the objective (233 in slice 2), under the 600 limit of constitution section 4. The Helm change removes the user-service hops env, and the values.yaml comment, deploy-aws.md, env descriptions, phase-08 and remediation plan document how to enable the check, the hop-count precondition, the B-4 release gate, the in-cluster trust caveat and why the gateway keeps SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none. Lookback still defaults to 0, so the check stays off. One minor doc defect: the env-reference generator now marks the referral salt and lookback as set by Helm because their names appear in a values.yaml comment, which contradicts the open TD-P8-24. The remaining nits do not block.
